title: Introduce stepped batching policy, quant-safety linter, and unit-econ smoke tests
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a stepped batching policy with conservative defaults, a static quantization-safety linter to catch incompatible quant profiles, and a new suite of unit-econ smoke tests for CI. No user-facing API changes; operational defaults improved.
description:
Motivation and summary:

We observed that single-threshold batching (max-batch-size only) can yield large cost variance across mixed workloads: small short requests suffer latency when waiting for large batch thresholds, but lowering thresholds increases per-token cost under high QPS. This PR introduces a small, operationally conservative stepped batching policy that trades off a couple of microseconds of scheduling overhead for much more stable unit economics across variable request size/QPS.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Implement 'stepped' batching policy in the serving runtime: the scheduler can be configured with an ordered list of candidate batch sizes (e.g., [1, 4, 16]) and per-step latency bounds. The runtime opportunistically serves smaller batches when latency SLOs are tight and ramps to larger steps when throughput allows.
- Add a `quant-safety` static linter that inspects quantization profiles and model graph ops to catch unsafe combinations (e.g., per-channel quant on ops we don't support in the CUDA/XT kernels, or FP16-only fused ops missing fallback). The linter emits warnings and suggested safe profiles.
- Add 'unit-econ smoke tests' to the CI: lightweight workload simulator that runs short generation workloads across a small matrix of batch sizes, quant profiles, and cache settings, and verifies cost-per-token regressions are within expected bands. Smoke tests run in ~8 minutes and gate regressions for perf/infra changes.

Implementation notes and commits (high-level):
- commit 1: runtime: stepped batcher core + scheduler hooks (api contract unchanged; new config block under route->batching)
- commit 2: runtime: careful backpressure handling and metrics (per-step latency histograms, step_transition_counter)
- commit 3: tooling: quant-safety linter as a CLI subcommand and CI check (bin/quant-linter)
- commit 4: tests: unit-econ smoke test harness + CI job + small golden baselines (ci/smoke/unit-econ/)

Files touched (high level):
- services/serve/scheduler/stepped_batcher.rs (new)
- services/serve/config/batching.yaml (docs + examples updated)
- runtime/metrics/registry.rs (added step-level metrics)
- tools/quant-linter/main.go (new)
- tools/quant-linter/rules/*.go (rules for op compatibility and fallbacks)
- ci/smoke/unit-econ/run_smoke.py (new harness)
- ci/.github/workflows/unit-econ-smoke.yml (CI job)
- sdk/python/examples/bench/stepped_batch_example.py (example config)
- docs/observability/batching.md (explain metrics and when to use stepped batching)
- tests/integration/serve/stepped_batcher_endtoend.test (integration test)

Small config example included in docs (snippet):

  batching:
    strategy: stepped
    steps:
      - size: 1
        max_latency_ms: 20
      - size: 4
        max_latency_ms: 50
      - size: 16
        max_latency_ms: 200

Notes on design choices: we intentionally keep the default step set conservative (1,4,16) to avoid surprising throughput regressions for large sustained QPS. The scheduler uses a tiny state machine to avoid flip-flopping between steps: a step transition requires a short stabilization window (configurable, default 50ms).

Quant-safety linter details:
- Static analysis of exported model graph + quant profile.
- Rules added: unsupported op-quant combos, precision funnel points (places where FP32->INT8 may lose critical dynamic range), and kernel mismatch with our CUDA kernels.
- Linter outputs machine-readable JSON and human-friendly summaries used by CI to annotate PRs. Example output: "WARN: op=matmul, quant=per_channel_int8 -> kernel_fallback_needed"

Unit-econ smoke tests:
- Simulate 1m equivalent tokens split across generated short (avg 12 tokens) and long (avg 160 tokens) requests to mimic chat + summarization mixes.
- Measure median latency, p95, and cost_per_1000_tokens. Failures trigger an artifact dump with token/time traces to help reproduce locally.

Review conversation (high-level transcript):
- Miguel: "Nice approach. Can we make the step list hierarchical per-route? Some customers want different steps for embeddings vs generation."
- Author (Asha): "Yes — config supports per-route batching blocks. Examples added to docs and example config file."
- Jade: "Quant-linter looks solid; add an allowlist for customers with known model exceptions."
- Author: "Added allowlist file support and tests for the allowlist behavior (tools/quant-linter/allowlist_test.go)."
- Evan: "CI time looks okay, but make sure smoke tests don't flake on low-QPS CI runners."
- Author: "Added retry + seeding and reduced variance; smoke runs ~8 minutes on our CI images."
- Miguel (approval): "Approve after green CI and one more perf run on canary infra."

CI summary: initial run had one transient failure in smoke tests on ubuntu-latest runner due to clock skew; rerun succeeded. All checks now green.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- No breaking API changes. The batching config is additive; if customers omit strategy, existing behavior (legacy max-batch-size) remains.
- Enabled stepped batching only when explicitly configured. We plan to roll out conservative defaults in the Dedicated face as an opt-in for early customers.

Testing and perf numbers (representative):
- Mixed workload (40% short, 60% long) on g4dn.xlarge: median latency improved ~6% vs single-threshold tuned for throughput and cost-per-token reduced ~12% compared to always-on small-batch strategy. p95 latency was within the configured budgets for the step set above.

Follow-ups and todos (post-merge):
- ENG-2101: automatic step-suggestor that profiles live traffic and proposes step tuples per-route.
- Add telemetry to Redwood Console to visualize step transition heatmaps per-route.
- Expand quant-linter rules to cover model conversion tooling and add auto-fix suggestions where safe.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Final merge commit: "squash: stepped batching + quant-linter + unit-econ CI (Asha Patel)"

If you want to run locally: see sdk/python/examples/bench/stepped_batch_example.py and tools/quant-linter/README.md for quickstart.
notes: This PR bundles runtime, tools, and CI changes to keep the feature integrated end-to-end. Kept scope tight to make reviewable while providing clear follow-ups for automatic tuning and Console UX.
